native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants shows a distinct prevalence style in low-elevation, human-modified and water-associated habitats — Urban, Riparian, Wetlands and Coastal — where it is both the dominant (or near-dominant) introduction pathway and spatially prevalent across plots: gardening accounts for 55.8% of non-native species occurrences in Wetlands and 53.5% in Coastal (majority pathway), 36.5% in Riparian (closest stream proximity, median 65 m), and is present in 47.7% of Urban plots (highest absolute load, 45 occurrences), while in Croplands the unintentional pathway dominates (gardening share 18.5%) and in natural/forested habitats (broad-leaved/coniferous forests, rock outcrops) non-native species are so rare (13 occurrences in 202 plots) that gardening is effectively absent.
